passage:
Class teacher's note, Grade 9B, 18 August.
Nazia and Bidisha have sat apart for about three weeks; Bidisha has looked more and more withdrawn. Today, as Nazia had asked, I let them use the empty art room during free period. I stayed at my desk at the far end, marking. Bidisha spoke first, quietly: "I felt left out at lunch. When you started sitting with the drama group." Her hands were shaking. Nazia looked shocked. "I thought you were angry about my birthday! I only sat there because they needed help with lines. I missed you." Bidisha laughed and then cried a little. Both seemed relieved, I think, that it was so small. Walking out, Nazia said, "Three weeks, for that." Plan: nothing further needed. Will keep an eye out.

qa.q: Where did Nazia and Bidisha talk?
qa.a: They talked in the empty art room during free period.

qa.q: What does Bidisha's laugh and small cry suggest?
qa.a: It suggests relief that the real reason was so small, after three weeks of fearing something worse.

qa.q: What lesson might both take from this?
qa.a: Saying "I felt left out" early would have cost a minute, while the silence cost three weeks of distance.

qa.q: What had Nazia believed the problem was?
qa.a: Nazia thought Bidisha was angry about the birthday, and had been missing Bidisha all along.

grounding: Shows a teen finally naming the hurt of being left out at lunch and finding the answer far smaller than the fear.

passage:
Wednesday
I did it. After two weeks of stomach-ache silence, I finally told Ishita. We were waiting for the school bus, and I said, really fast, "I felt left out when you went to the mall with Pihu and didn't ask me." My face was burning. I was ready for her to say I was being clingy, or that she didn't want me there. Instead she just said, "Oh no, I thought you had dance class. I'm so sorry." That was it! Two weeks of imagining the worst, and the real answer took ten seconds. We shared her earphones all the way home. Note to self: next time, say it on day one, not day fourteen.
— Aditi

qa.q: Where were they when Aditi finally spoke?
qa.a: They were waiting for the school bus.

qa.q: What was Aditi afraid Ishita would say?
qa.a: Aditi feared Ishita would call it clingy or say she didn't want Aditi there.

qa.q: What note does Aditi make for next time, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Say it on day one, not day fourteen, because the real answer was small and the silence cost two weeks of worry.

qa.q: How might Ishita have felt hearing about the mall trip?
qa.a: Ishita was probably surprised and sorry, since she truly thought Aditi had dance class. 😊

grounding: Shows a teen speaking the real hurt of being left out, getting a reply much smaller than feared, and resolving to speak up earlier.
